subject: Mutual Action Plan recap: Redwood <> Acme - next steps & timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan recap: Redwood <> Acme - next steps & timeline

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed mutual action plan so we have alignment on stakeholders, milestones, and decision criteria. Please reply with any edits.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on peak traffic windows affecting search relevance and user sessions (esp. East Coast mornings).
- Embedding costs have grown 3x year-over-year; team needs predictable unit economics and caching.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + customer-managed KMS required for pilot.

Goals for pilot
1) Validate query latency below 120ms p95 at 10 req/s baseline
2) Reduce per-embedding cost via caching & batching by 30%
3) Demonstrate SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration for legal/procurement

Proposed MAP (milestones & dates)
- Week 1 (Feb 22–26): Provision dedicated trial environment + KMS test account (Acme infra team)
- Week 2 (Mar 1–5): Baseline performance run; initial model suggestion & quantization profile (Redwood)
- Week 3 (Mar 8–12): Integration test with embeddings cache and request routing; measure cost/latency delta
- Week 4 (Mar 15–19): Executive review; procurement decision & contract signature target

Stakeholders & roles
- Acme: Tom Reynolds (dir. of search, decision-maker), Priya Shah (engineering lead), Khaled Mansour (security/compliance)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, owner), Vivek Kulkarni (solutions engineer), Rachel Kim (customer success)

Decision process
- Technical sign-off by Priya/engineering on Mar 12
- Security sign-off by Khaled on Mar 12
- Executive approval (Tom) target Mar 19

Open items / asks for Acme
- Access to a KMS test key by Feb 24
- A short dataset (5000 sample queries) for baseline run by Mar 1

Next steps (I will)
- Share a formal MAP spreadsheet attached (ACME-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a Doc with timelines
- Schedule a kickoff session with Vivek and Priya for Feb 23 at 10am PT — can you confirm availability?

Attachment: ACME-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Khaled Mansour <khaled.mansour@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan recap: Redwood <> Acme - next steps & timeline

Marissa —

Thanks for the very clear recap. This looks right from our side; a few clarifications below.

- Latency: priority is p95 under 120ms but we need to ensure p99 behavior documented for spikes. Can your team include p99 monitoring hooks?
- Timeline: Procurement needs a week to review contract language. If everything looks ok after the technical run, procurement will expect a contract ready to sign around Mar 26 (so executive approval could be Mar 26 instead of Mar 19).
- KMS: Khaled will provide a test key this week (Khaled, can you confirm ETA?).

We're okay with the kickoff on Feb 23 at 10am PT — Priya and I will join.

I added Priya and Khaled to this thread so they have visibility. Also looping in our procurement contact, Molly (copied), for later.

Thanks,
Tom
